https://www.baltictimes.com/lithuania_jo.text: Estonia Latvia Lithuania Business Analysis Opinions Culture EU Affairs Search Archive Lithuania joins fund to preserve Ukrainian cultural heritage damaged by Russia 2026-08-05 BNS/TBT Staff VILNIUS - Lithuania is joining the International Fund for Ukrainian Cultural Heritage, dedicated to preserving and restoring sites damaged by Russian aggression, Culture Minister Lukas Alsys said on Wednesday during a meeting with his Ukrainian counterpart Tetjana Berezna in Ukraine. According to the ministry, the fund has already contributed to the restoration of key Ukrainian cultural sites, with new projects planned for the future. Alsys said Lithuania's participation was an expression of solidarity and concrete support for Ukraine's cultural heritage. The meeting focused on protecting cultural assets during wartime, international cooperation, and combating Russian propaganda and disinformation. Both sides agreed to strengthen cooperation by sharing expertise and increasing public resilience to information threats. The ministers also discussed preparations for Lithuania's presidency of the Council of the European Union in 2027. Lithuania aims to actively involve Ukraine in meetings of culture ministers and other events under the presidency programme, promoting joint European cultural projects and institutional cooperation between museums, theatres and other cultural institutions. According to the ministry, the visit to Kyiv reaffirmed Lithuania's firm support for Ukraine and the determination of both countries to jointly protect cultural heritage and develop a long-term strategic partnership. http://astanatimes.com/2026/09/kazakhsta.text: Friday, 9 October, 2026 Almaty 64 °F / 18 °C Astana 48 °F / 9 °C All Stories Nation Astana Culture Sports People Kazakhstan Regions State of the Nation Election 2022 Election 2023 International Astana International Forum Kazakhstan’s Presidency in SCO 5th World Nomad Games Business Central Asia Opinions All Stories Nation Astana Culture Sports People Kazakhstan Regions State of the Nation Election 2022 Election 2023 International Astana International Forum Kazakhstan’s Presidency in SCO 5th World Nomad Games Business Central Asia Opinions Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Expands Bilateral Ties at UN General Assembly By Dana Omirgazy in Editor’s Picks , International on 24 September 2026 ASTANA – Kazakhstan has launched an active diplomatic agenda at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, with Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi holding talks with counterparts from several countries and discussing global peace, security and humanitarian law on Sept. 23 in New York. Kazakhstan’s Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi. Photo credit: Kazakh Foreign Ministry Expanding bilateral partnerships On the first day of the General Assembly’s High-Level Week in New York, Tileuberdi held talks with his counterparts from Hungary, Moldova, Poland, Slovenia, Ukraine and El Salvador, the ministry’s press service reported. The discussions focused on bilateral cooperation, prospects for expanding political dialogue and trade and economic ties, as well as key international and regional topics. Tileuberdi also met with UN Under-Secretary-General and UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) Executive Director Rebecca Grynspan, a candidate for UN Secretary-General, and UNESCO Director-General Khaled El-Enany. The meetings addressed ways to strengthen cooperation with UN institutions and improve the effectiveness of multilateral mechanisms. Focus on peace and security Tileuberdi also took part in a high-level discussion, Reaffirming the Promise of Peace: Using the Power We Have, which focused on conflict prevention and resolution, preventive diplomacy, mediation and strengthening partnerships within the international system. Participants exchanged views on strengthening the UN’s role in maintaining international peace and security and using existing mechanisms more effectively to settle disputes peacefully. New diplomatic relations An important outcome of the first day was the establishment of diplomatic relations between Kazakhstan and the Central African Republic. The two countries’ foreign ministers signed a joint communiqué confirming their interest in developing bilateral ties and cooperation on international platforms. Tileuberdi also participated in a working meeting of foreign ministers of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) member states, where participants discussed priorities for cooperation between the CSTO and the UN. Kazakhstan promotes compliance with Humanitarian Law At a separate meeting with foreign ministers of the founding states of the Global Initiative to Strengthen Political Commitment to International Humanitarian Law (IHL) and International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) President Mirjana Spoljaric, Tileuberdi stressed that the effectiveness of international humanitarian law should be measured by its ability to protect civilians and medical and humanitarian personnel, safeguard critical civilian infrastructure and ensure the delivery of humanitarian assistance. The meeting brought together the founding states – Kazakhstan, Brazil, China, France, Jordan and South Africa – to discuss preparations for the Humanity in War high-level conference, scheduled for Dec. 7 in Jordan. Tileuberdi emphasized that international humanitarian law must be applied universally, consistently and in good faith, without selectivity or politicization. Following the meeting, the founding states and the ICRC called on the international community to join the Initiative, strengthen compliance with international humanitarian law and ensure high-level participation at the upcoming conference in Jordan. Celebrating its 95th anniversary this year, Exeter-headquartered South West Metal Finishing (SWMF, United Kingdom) has recognized more than 30 long-serving employees who, together, bring a combined 700 years of service to the business.

Established in 1931, SWMF provides precision surface treatments and finishing services for equipment used across the aerospace, defense, nuclear and engineering sectors. The company employs 200 people across four sites in Marsh Barton, Exeter Airport, Yeovil and Chippenham. Its workforce has tallied an estimated 1,300 years of combined experience. With around 30 employees joining in the past year alone, the recent awards reflect the company’s mix of longstanding expertise and new talent.

Among the long-service honorees is Kevin Baker, who celebrates 47 years with the company. Over a career that included roles overseeing compliance, quality, chemistry and the safe handling of materials that surface treatment depends on, Baker rose to become managing director. Now semi-retired, he leads SWMF’s apprenticeship program alongside chemist Gary Ridgway, guiding new intakes through training.

“Having hundreds of years of experience across our team, with so many colleagues staying with us for decades, is quite special in this day and age,” says Damon Gill, group managing director at SWMF. “Surface finishing is a highly specialist, critical industry where expertise is hard to come by. These aren’t skills you can learn from a manual — they’re high-level standards handed down person to person over decades.”

“That’s why bringing in apprentices and continually developing our team is so important,” Gill continues. “It’s about passing specialist knowledge to the next generation. Having Kevin lead our apprenticeship scheme brings that full circle. We bring five trainees through a year and when they visit customer sites to see where the parts end up — whether that’s Boeing, Airbus or Leonardo Helicopters — something clicks. When you nurture that talent early and show people there is no ceiling on their progression, they stay and feel they can build long-term careers.”

The long-service group spans every part of the business, and three of its members illustrate the range of routes people take into surface engineering.

At the Exeter Airport paint division, production manager Janos Zombor arrived in the U.K. from Hungary in 2007 and spent his early working life as a chef. He joined SWMF in 2014 as a production operative, moved into spray painting within six months and trained across every process in the business before becoming a quality inspector and, in April 2026, production manager.

In Yeovil, site manager Dave Barton joined in 2005 at age 20, when the site was still known as Reid Plating and working largely in zinc. He was made supervisor after five or six years, spent time in quality and inspection and took on management of the site in late 2017 after having turned the role down twice.

At Chippenham, office, accounts and personnel manager Sarah-Jayne Bell marks 34 years in October. She joined at 18 on a work placement, started in admin and accounting on a typewriter and has since worked across personnel, data and analysis, customer quoting and account management, playing a central role in digitizing the site’s processes.

The 95th anniversary comes alongside a continued commitment to developing new talent. SWMF launched its apprenticeship scheme immediately after the pandemic — having retained its entire workforce through it — to build skills in a trade where experienced electroplaters are notoriously hard to find. Five apprentices are being recruited in 2026, with the plan working closely with local colleges and schools and taking apprentices out to customer sites so they can see firsthand where the parts they treat end up. The program is now being extended to include further qualifications, with no ceiling on advancement within the business.

Three of SWMF’s sites are NADCAP gold accredited, meaning the company has demonstrated exceptional, long-term compliance and superior performance during specialized aerospace and defense audits.

SWMF is currently recruiting across all four sites and is particularly seeking candidates with experience in electroplating, anodizing, NDT and paint spraying. For more information, email contact@swmf.co.uk or visit www.swmf.co.uk.
